notes: Valve Source RCON (AMP's template sets AdminMethod=SourceRCON and the reference client uses packet types 0x02/0x03). Enable it either with launch arguments -EnableRCON -RCONPort=7779 -RCONPassword=<pw> (-RCONIP, -RCONMaxActiveConnections also exist) or in HarshDoorstop/Saved/Config/<Platform>/Game.ini under [/Script/RCON.RCONServerSystem] with bEnabled=True, ListenPort=7779, Password=, MaxActiveConnections=, MaxAuthAttempts=. The setting names here are the ini ones; the launch-argument spellings are RCONPort/RCONPassword. There is no dedicated roster command in the reference client: 'status' returns a header block (Server Name / Local Address / Map / Game Mode / hibernation / match and session state / 'N Human Players, N Bots, N Spectators') followed by one row per player as '<PlayerID> <Name> <SteamID64 or BOT>', which is what listPlayers parses. DISAGREEMENT: Legion Hosting's admin guide lists 'ListPlayers', 'Kick <PlayerID>', 'Ban <PlayerID>'; a Steam discussion and BisectHosting list only 'kick <Username>' and 'ban <Username>'. The @ohd-tools/rcon client, the only source that shows literal wire text, sends kick "<name>" "<reason>" / kickId <id> "<reason>" and ban "<name>" "<reason>" <duration> / banId <id> "<reason>" <duration>, and its parser matches the server's own replies ("Player with id number 'N' was successfully kicked from the server with reason '...'"), which confirms the server accepts both a name and a numeric in-session player ID. The numeric ID form is used here because 'status' hands it to us directly and names with spaces are fragile; substitute {playerName} into the quoted-name form if you prefer. Ban duration units are contested inside that same client: the method doc-comment says seconds while its default message and the server's success reply both say minutes - minutes is assumed, 0 = permanent. No unban command was found on any source; bans persist in Bans.cfg alongside Admins.cfg and MapCycle.cfg, but no source gave a confirmed path or line format, so no banList is recorded rather than guessing one. Confidence is low because the exact command text rests on a single project's source code and the hosting-side docs contradict it.
